summary: Kept the night-search for lodging as a near-verbatim sequence (Crossed Harpoons, Sword-Fish, the Trap, the Spouter Inn sign) and the Euroclydon/Lazarus-and-Dives meditation, trimming the Nantucket history, the Dives-temperance conceit and some descriptive padding.
acceptable_changes: Cut the Nantucket cobblestone anecdote and Red-Men aside as historical color not needed for plot.
Cut the closing Dives-as-Czar/temperance-society paragraph; the Lazarus and Dives contrast is already fully established in the retained text.
Elided boot-sole and house-description detail that repeats the cold and poverty already conveyed.
risks: Lazarus/Dives passage is compressed by whole-sentence cuts; the social-satire strand is somewhat thinner.
'Paul's tossed craft' allusion retained without gloss, per the period-allusion rule.
Chapter is near target but the Nantucket motivation is shortened, so New Bedford as an unwanted stopover is less elaborated.
review_focus: Verify the retained Euroclydon black-letter quotation and 'these eyes are windows' passage are verbatim.
Check the transition from Lazarus to 'But no more of this blubbering' still reads naturally after the Dives-as-Czar paragraph was cut.
